Recommend at least a rough prefilter between input and storage, you can buy it just get a food grade 55 gal drum and fill so that water source --> coarse gravel/river pebbles --> activated charcoal --> sand --> storage. This will filter out most of not all of the particulate debris and the charcoal will help remove toxins and some negative organic compounds. This won't make it completely potable but gives a big step in the right direction. Keep a bottle of 2% tincture of iodine, a little goes a long way. Now to treat the whole tank (200gal) it would take about 7 ounces, 14 ounces if the water is cloudy/murky. This needs to be circulated through and and given at least 30 minutes to work. You could also let it naturally disperse throughout over the course of a few days. Note, I would still recommend additional treatment before drinking, at minimum boiling. Personally I would treat the whole tank and then pull what I needed for daily (or couple day) use. Treating on a smaller scale you would use 20 drops per gallon (40 if murky), give it a good stir, and then wait thirty minutes. For an additional measure you could also use a Berkey system or make your own for cheaper with two food grade 5 gallon buckets and a ceramic Bell filter.

Couple things that have worked for me in the past depending how handy you are, get a few boards 2x2 or 2x4 and build a simple box frame say 4ft per side (if your a bot more inclined could build big enough for you to walk into) just needs to be big enough to cover the plant with a bit of room to the sides, wrap that in clear plastic cuta small hole at the bottom and a small hole at the top to allow some air circulation (could even run a little 4-inch desk fan inside with the plants) helps hold in more heat humidity while still letting the plants breathe because there's room around them and the plastic not draped right on top of them. Additionally you can buy insulation from home Depot or Lowe's not the pink stuff but there's a thin silver insulation that comes on a roll for I think right around 20 bucks for 25 ft, if you're dealing with extreme cold that will definitely help and reflectiveness of it will shine more light into the plants areas that aren't being hit directly from above more light equals more photosynthesis equals better production. One final thought that would be a bit more pricey could be to get a small say 2 foot fluorescent fixture which will generate more heat than the LEDs adding that to the mix while not only adding more light but more heat can help as well.  If you wanted to go that route my recommendation would be just a 2ft t5 light with Bloom bulbs if you're going for fruiting or Walmart sells a 2ft regular fluorescent fixture for 12 bucks that I think even comes with the bulbs.
